title: CmdPal: Provider initialization runs outside the startup timeout (EXT26.S2)

evidence: The issue reports an isolated shortened-budget test in which InitializeWithHost exceeded the activation deadline.
The report explicitly says no native COM call was hung.
Current TryStartExtensionAsync awaits StartExtensionAsync with WaitAsync before synchronously constructing CommandProviderWrapper.
judgment.recommended_action: Use the targeted maintainer reproduction to validate the proposed mechanism before design approval; no upstream action has been taken.
judgment.rationale: A shortened-budget test reproduced initialization exceeding the activation deadline while another provider was healthy. The current source wraps activation in WaitAsync before constructing the provider synchronously; a hung native COM call was not reproduced.

fix_assessment.rationale: No matching fix was found by focused issue-number search; treat the reported mechanism as a hypothesis and validate before implementation.

verification: Block InitializeWithHost past the deadline while a healthy provider starts; verify healthy startup completes within budget.
Release the blocked call after timeout and verify its obsolete result is not published.
Run focused service tests for ownership and repeated initialization.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The timeout covers activation but not provider construction and InitializeWithHost; a blocking initialization can hold startup beyond the deadline, and timeout does not cancel the COM call.
plan: Define the deadline over activation and provider initialization, keeping potentially blocking COM work off the UI thread.
Track in-flight initialization after timeout; do not treat WaitAsync timeout as cancellation.
Retire late results when their load lifetime is obsolete and keep healthy providers progressing.
Add timeout, late-result and healthy-peer tests.

confidence.rationale: The shortened-budget test verifies the gap, but safe ownership and cleanup of still-running COM initialization are not tested.
